title: Listen for the third voice
summary: Sit outside and notice birdsong, distant calls and quieter sounds without identifying species.
steps: Choose a familiar outdoor spot where you can stay comfortably.
Notice three separate sounds. Let the closest one pass, then listen farther away.
Keep one sound in mind; your field note can wait until you return.
notePrompt: Which sound surprised you?

title: Follow one cloud
summary: Watch a small piece of the sky change shape, light or colour while resting outdoors.
setting: somewhere with a view of the sky
steps: Pick a comfortable outdoor place with a view of the sky.
Choose one patch of cloud or open sky and notice what changes.
Look away from the screen until you are ready to come back.
notePrompt: What changed in the sky?

title: Find a texture trio
summary: Look closely at bark, stone and another outdoor surface; compare patterns without taking samples.
steps: Head to a familiar outdoor place and leave everything where it is.
Notice three different surfaces: lines, cracks, smooth patches or tiny shadows.
Choose the pattern you would want to sketch from memory.
notePrompt: Which texture would you draw?

title: Meet one tree from below
summary: Observe the silhouette, canopy and moving leaves of a nearby tree from a stationary place.
setting: near a tree you can observe comfortably
steps: Choose a place where you can comfortably see a nearby tree.
Trace its outline with your eyes, then notice a smaller branch.
Watch which leaves move first when the air changes.
notePrompt: What detail made this tree different?

title: Take a one-colour walk
summary: Follow a familiar short walk while noticing every outdoor appearance of one colour.
steps: Pick one colour before putting the phone away.
Take your usual short walk and notice where that colour appears.
Return with three colour memories, rather than a set of photos.
notePrompt: Where did your colour appear?

title: Watch the shadow edges
summary: Look for edges, gaps and overlapping shapes in outdoor shadows when they are present.
steps: Choose an outdoor place where shadows are visible.
Find a sharp edge and a soft edge. Notice what casts each one.
Watch one edge for a little while without needing to measure it.
notePrompt: What made the most interesting shadow?

title: Notice a garden's new detail
summary: Spend a few quiet minutes observing leaves, buds and changes in a garden or planter without plant-care instructions.
setting: a garden, balcony planter or public planting
steps: Choose a planting you are allowed to observe.
Compare two leaves or buds. Notice differences in colour, size or shape.
Leave the plants undisturbed and remember one detail.
notePrompt: What did you notice that you usually miss?

title: Look near, then farther
summary: Rest outside while comparing one nearby detail with something farther away in the same view.
steps: Stay at a comfortable outdoor spot.
Notice a nearby texture, then a farther shape, then the whole view.
Repeat at your own pace and leave the phone in your pocket.
notePrompt: Which part of the view held your attention?

title: Find the city's repeating pattern
summary: Take a short familiar walk to notice repeating bricks, windows, railings or paving designs.
setting: a familiar pavement or pedestrian area
steps: Use a familiar outdoor pedestrian area.
Notice something that repeats, then one small variation in that pattern.
Remember the variation as your discovery.
notePrompt: Where did the pattern break?

title: Make a leaf palette in your head
summary: Look at different leaf colours outdoors without picking leaves or identifying a plant.
steps: Choose a place with leaves you can see clearly.
Notice three shades, even if all three look green at first.
Give each shade your own name and leave the leaves in place.
notePrompt: What were your three colour names?

title: Find what the air moves
summary: Watch outdoor movement in leaves, grass, fabric or clouds without needing a weather forecast.
setting: any outdoor spot with something moving
steps: Choose a comfortable outside spot.
Notice one thing that moves with the air and one that stays still.
Watch how their movement changes for a few minutes.
notePrompt: What moved most subtly?

title: Frame a picture without taking it
summary: Find an outdoor composition of foreground, middle distance and background, with no camera required.
steps: Go to a familiar outdoor place and look for a view you enjoy.
Notice the nearest shape, the middle of the scene and its background.
Keep the picture as a memory instead of reaching for a camera.
notePrompt: What belonged in your frame?

title: Notice life at a smaller scale
summary: Observe small outdoor movement on a tree, wall or planting without disturbing wildlife.
setting: near a surface or planting you can observe
steps: Choose a place where you can watch a small outdoor surface.
Look for movement or traces of activity without touching or disturbing anything.
A quiet moment with no movement is also a valid observation.
notePrompt: What small detail showed activity?

title: Take your usual way, notice one new thing
summary: Walk a familiar short loop and pay attention to an ordinary detail you have overlooked.
steps: Choose a short route you already know.
Notice one new detail at the beginning, middle and end.
Return by your familiar route; the app does not choose directions for you.
notePrompt: Which ordinary detail felt new?

title: Listen to the water from your place
summary: Notice a fountain, rain or other visible water from an established comfortable viewing place.
setting: a comfortable place where water is already visible or audible
steps: Stay at a familiar viewing place where you can already see or hear water.
Notice the rhythm, reflections or gaps between sounds.
Keep the observation simple and leave the water undisturbed.
notePrompt: What rhythm or reflection did you notice?

title: Collect five lines with your eyes
summary: Notice straight, curved and branching outdoor lines as a small creative observation exercise.
steps: Look around from a comfortable outdoor spot.
Find five different lines: a branch, edge, crack, curve or horizon.
Choose two that would make an interesting sketch later.
notePrompt: Which two lines would you sketch?

title: Swap one small discovery
summary: Take a familiar short walk with a companion and each point out one overlooked outdoor detail.
setting: a familiar place with your companion
steps: Choose a familiar short walk together.
Each person notices a detail without turning it into a competition.
Share the discoveries near the end, then put the phone away again.
notePrompt: What did someone else notice first?

title: Give your outside spot five minutes
summary: Observe the sky, sound and movement from a balcony, doorway or another comfortable outdoor spot.
steps: Choose a place outside where you can stay comfortably.
Notice one sound, one shape and one movement.
You do not need to travel anywhere to make an observation.
notePrompt: Which of the three stayed with you?

title: Find a sign of the season
summary: Notice leaves, light, buds or other ordinary outdoor details that suggest seasonal change.
steps: Take a short familiar walk or explore a place you know.
Notice one sign of change in plants or light without naming a species.
Compare it with what you remember from another day.
notePrompt: What sign of change did you find?

title: Notice a quiet corner
summary: Spend a short time outdoors in a familiar comfortable spot and attend to ordinary details without a task list.
steps: Choose a familiar outside place where you feel comfortable staying.
Notice details at your own pace; there is nothing to finish or identify.
Come back when you want, with one small memory if you like.
notePrompt: What detail stayed with you?
